For most of my life, my answer to how are you was the same. Fine, busy, you know. It was never true, and nobody expected it to be. Last year I tried an experiment. When a friend asked, I gave one honest sentence. I have been feeling a bit run down lately, to be honest. That was all. No long story, no complaining. What surprised me was the reaction. People did not run away. Most of them answered with something honest of their own. One friend told me she had been sleeping badly for months and had not told anyone. One sentence opened a real conversation. I still say fine to the cashier at the supermarket. But with people who matter, I give the honest version, and I keep it short.

I used to think rest was what happened when the work was finished. The problem is that the work is never finished. After two years of that, I was completely burned out, and it took my doctor to say it out loud. These days I treat recharging as part of the job. I have been doing three small things for about a year now. I walk for twenty minutes after lunch. I switch off my work phone at seven. And on Sundays I do something with my hands, usually cooking. None of this is dramatic. But my energy is better than it has been in ten years, and I have not been ill once since March. The lesson is simple. Pace yourself, or your body will do it for you.

First, I give one honest sentence: to be honest, I've been feeling a bit run down. Then I give the reason: I've been working late, and it's taking a toll on my sleep. After that, I say what I've been doing about it, like switching off my phone at eight. Next, I ask about the other person: how have you been feeling lately? In the end, I offer one gentle piece of advice, or I simply listen.
